from lfx.base.data.utils import IMG_FILE_TYPES, TEXT_FILE_TYPES
from lfx.base.io.chat import ChatComponent
from lfx.inputs.inputs import BoolInput
from lfx.io import (
    DropdownInput,
    FileInput,
    MessageTextInput,
    MultilineInput,
    Output,
)
from lfx.schema.message import Message
from lfx.utils.constants import (
    MESSAGE_SENDER_AI,
    MESSAGE_SENDER_NAME_USER,
    MESSAGE_SENDER_USER,
)


class ChatInput(ChatComponent):
    display_name = "Chat Input"
    description = "Get chat inputs from the Playground."
    documentation: str = "https://docs.langflow.org/chat-input-and-output"
    icon = "MessagesSquare"
    name = "ChatInput"
    minimized = True

    inputs = [
        MultilineInput(
            name="input_value",
            display_name="Input Text",
            value="",
            info="Message to be passed as input.",
            input_types=[],
        ),
        BoolInput(
            name="should_store_message",
            display_name="Store Messages",
            info="Store the message in the history.",
            value=True,
            advanced=True,
        ),
        DropdownInput(
            name="sender",
            display_name="Sender Type",
            options=[MESSAGE_SENDER_AI, MESSAGE_SENDER_USER],
            value=MESSAGE_SENDER_USER,
            info="Type of sender.",
            advanced=True,
        ),
        MessageTextInput(
            name="sender_name",
            display_name="Sender Name",
            info="Name of the sender.",
            value=MESSAGE_SENDER_NAME_USER,
            advanced=True,
        ),
        MessageTextInput(
            name="session_id",
            display_name="Session ID",
            info="The session ID of the chat. If empty, the current session ID parameter will be used.",
            advanced=True,
        ),
        MessageTextInput(
            name="context_id",
            display_name="Context ID",
            info="The context ID of the chat. Adds an extra layer to the local memory.",
            value="",
            advanced=True,
        ),
        FileInput(
            name="files",
            display_name="Files",
            file_types=TEXT_FILE_TYPES + IMG_FILE_TYPES,
            info="Files to be sent with the message.",
            advanced=True,
            is_list=True,
            temp_file=True,
        ),
    ]
    outputs = [
        Output(display_name="Chat Message", name="message", method="message_response"),
    ]

    async def message_response(self) -> Message:
        # Ensure files is a list and filter out empty/None values
        files = self.files if self.files else []
        if files and not isinstance(files, list):
            files = [files]
        # Filter out None/empty values
        files = [f for f in files if f is not None and f != ""]

        session_id = self.session_id or self.graph.session_id or ""
        message = await Message.create(
            text=self.input_value,
            sender=self.sender,
            sender_name=self.sender_name,
            session_id=session_id,
            context_id=self.context_id,
            files=files,
        )
        if session_id and isinstance(message, Message) and self.should_store_message:
            stored_message = await self.send_message(
                message,
            )
            self.message.value = stored_message
            message = stored_message

        self.status = message
        return message

from collections.abc import Generator
from typing import Any

import orjson
from fastapi.encoders import jsonable_encoder

from lfx.base.io.chat import ChatComponent
from lfx.helpers.data import safe_convert
from lfx.inputs.inputs import BoolInput, DropdownInput, HandleInput, MessageTextInput
from lfx.schema.data import Data
from lfx.schema.dataframe import DataFrame
from lfx.schema.message import Message
from lfx.schema.properties import Source
from lfx.template.field.base import Output
from lfx.utils.constants import (
    MESSAGE_SENDER_AI,
    MESSAGE_SENDER_NAME_AI,
    MESSAGE_SENDER_USER,
)


class ChatOutput(ChatComponent):
    display_name = "Chat Output"
    description = "Display a chat message in the Playground."
    documentation: str = "https://docs.langflow.org/chat-input-and-output"
    icon = "MessagesSquare"
    name = "ChatOutput"
    minimized = True

    inputs = [
        HandleInput(
            name="input_value",
            display_name="Inputs",
            info="Message to be passed as output.",
            input_types=["Data", "JSON", "DataFrame", "Table", "Message"],
            required=True,
        ),
        BoolInput(
            name="should_store_message",
            display_name="Store Messages",
            info="Store the message in the history.",
            value=True,
            advanced=True,
        ),
        DropdownInput(
            name="sender",
            display_name="Sender Type",
            options=[MESSAGE_SENDER_AI, MESSAGE_SENDER_USER],
            value=MESSAGE_SENDER_AI,
            advanced=True,
            info="Type of sender.",
        ),
        MessageTextInput(
            name="sender_name",
            display_name="Sender Name",
            info="Name of the sender.",
            value=MESSAGE_SENDER_NAME_AI,
            advanced=True,
        ),
        MessageTextInput(
            name="session_id",
            display_name="Session ID",
            info="The session ID of the chat. If empty, the current session ID parameter will be used.",
            advanced=True,
        ),
        MessageTextInput(
            name="context_id",
            display_name="Context ID",
            info="The context ID of the chat. Adds an extra layer to the local memory.",
            value="",
            advanced=True,
        ),
        MessageTextInput(
            name="data_template",
            display_name="Data Template",
            value="{text}",
            advanced=True,
            info="Template to convert Data to Text. If left empty, it will be dynamically set to the Data's text key.",
        ),
        BoolInput(
            name="clean_data",
            display_name="Basic Clean Data",
            value=True,
            advanced=True,
            info="Whether to clean data before converting to string.",
        ),
    ]
    outputs = [
        Output(
            display_name="Output Message",
            name="message",
            method="message_response",
        ),
    ]

    def _build_source(self, id_: str | None, display_name: str | None, source: str | None) -> Source:
        source_dict = {}
        if id_:
            source_dict["id"] = id_
        if display_name:
            source_dict["display_name"] = display_name
        if source:
            # Handle case where source is a ChatOpenAI object
            if hasattr(source, "model_name"):
                source_dict["source"] = source.model_name
            elif hasattr(source, "model"):
                source_dict["source"] = str(source.model)
            else:
                source_dict["source"] = str(source)
        return Source(**source_dict)

    async def message_response(self) -> Message:
        # First convert the input to string if needed
        text = self.convert_to_string()

        # Get source properties
        source, _, display_name, source_id = self.get_properties_from_source_component()

        # Create or use existing Message object
        if isinstance(self.input_value, Message) and not self.is_connected_to_chat_input():
            message = self.input_value
            # Update message properties
            message.text = text
            # Preserve existing session_id from the incoming message if it exists
            existing_session_id = message.session_id
        else:
            message = Message(text=text)
            existing_session_id = None

        # Set message properties
        message.sender = self.sender
        message.sender_name = self.sender_name
        # Preserve session_id from incoming message, or use component/graph session_id
        message.session_id = (
            self.session_id or existing_session_id or (self.graph.session_id if hasattr(self, "graph") else None) or ""
        )
        message.context_id = self.context_id
        message.flow_id = self.graph.flow_id if hasattr(self, "graph") else None
        message.properties.source = self._build_source(source_id, display_name, source)

        # Store message if needed
        if message.session_id and self.should_store_message:
            stored_message = await self.send_message(message)
            self.message.value = stored_message
            message = stored_message

        # Set accumulated token usage from all upstream LLM vertices.
        # This must happen AFTER send_message() because streaming captures
        # usage from chunks and would overwrite accumulated totals.
        if hasattr(self, "_vertex") and self._vertex is not None:
            accumulated_usage = self._vertex._accumulate_upstream_token_usage()  # noqa: SLF001
            if accumulated_usage:
                message.properties.usage = accumulated_usage
                if self.should_store_message and message.get_id():
                    message = await self._update_stored_message(message)
                    await self._send_message_event(message, id_=message.get_id())

        self.status = message
        return message

    def _serialize_data(self, data: Data) -> str:
        """Serialize Data object to JSON string."""
        # Convert data.data to JSON-serializable format
        serializable_data = jsonable_encoder(data.data)
        # Serialize with orjson, enabling pretty printing with indentation
        json_bytes = orjson.dumps(serializable_data, option=orjson.OPT_INDENT_2)
        # Convert bytes to string and wrap in Markdown code blocks
        return "```json\n" + json_bytes.decode("utf-8") + "\n```"

    def _validate_input(self) -> None:
        """Validate the input data and raise ValueError if invalid."""
        if self.input_value is None:
            msg = "Input data cannot be None"
            raise ValueError(msg)
        if isinstance(self.input_value, list) and not all(
            isinstance(item, Message | Data | DataFrame | str) for item in self.input_value
        ):
            invalid_types = [
                type(item).__name__
                for item in self.input_value
                if not isinstance(item, Message | Data | DataFrame | str)
            ]
            msg = f"Expected Data or DataFrame or Message or str, got {invalid_types}"
            raise TypeError(msg)
        if not isinstance(
            self.input_value,
            Message | Data | DataFrame | str | list | Generator | type(None),
        ):
            type_name = type(self.input_value).__name__
            msg = f"Expected Data or DataFrame or Message or str, Generator or None, got {type_name}"
            raise TypeError(msg)

    def convert_to_string(self) -> str | Generator[Any, None, None]:
        """Convert input data to string with proper error handling."""
        self._validate_input()
        if isinstance(self.input_value, list):
            clean_data: bool = getattr(self, "clean_data", False)
            return "\n".join([safe_convert(item, clean_data=clean_data) for item in self.input_value])
        if isinstance(self.input_value, Generator):
            return self.input_value
        return safe_convert(self.input_value)

from lfx.base.models.model import LCModelComponent
from lfx.base.models.unified_models import (
    get_language_model_options,
    get_llm,
    handle_model_input_update,
)
from lfx.base.models.watsonx_constants import IBM_WATSONX_URLS
from lfx.components.models_and_agents.model_selection import apply_model_overrides
from lfx.field_typing.constants import LanguageModel
from lfx.field_typing.range_spec import RangeSpec
from lfx.inputs.inputs import BoolInput, DropdownInput, StrInput
from lfx.io import IntInput, MessageInput, ModelInput, MultilineInput, SecretStrInput, SliderInput

DEFAULT_OLLAMA_URL = "http://localhost:11434"


class LanguageModelComponent(LCModelComponent):
    display_name = "Language Model"
    description = "Runs a language model given a specified provider."
    documentation: str = "https://docs.langflow.org/components-models"
    icon = "brain-circuit"
    category = "models"

    inputs = [
        ModelInput(
            name="model",
            display_name="Language Model",
            info="Select your model provider",
            real_time_refresh=True,
            required=True,
        ),
        StrInput(
            name="model_name",
            display_name="Model Name Override",
            info=(
                "Optional model name to use instead of the selected model. "
                "Can be set from a global variable for runtime model selection."
            ),
            advanced=True,
            load_from_db=False,
        ),
        StrInput(
            name="provider",
            display_name="Provider Override",
            info=(
                "Optional provider to use with Model Name Override. Leave blank to use the selected model's provider."
            ),
            advanced=True,
            load_from_db=False,
        ),
        SecretStrInput(
            name="api_key",
            display_name="API Key",
            info="Overrides global provider settings. Leave blank to use your pre-configured API Key.",
            required=False,
            show=True,
            real_time_refresh=True,
            advanced=True,
        ),
        DropdownInput(
            name="base_url_ibm_watsonx",
            display_name="watsonx API Endpoint",
            info="The base URL of the API (IBM watsonx.ai only)",
            options=IBM_WATSONX_URLS,
            value=IBM_WATSONX_URLS[0],
            combobox=True,
            show=False,
            real_time_refresh=True,
        ),
        StrInput(
            name="project_id",
            display_name="watsonx Project ID",
            info="The project ID associated with the foundation model (IBM watsonx.ai only)",
            show=False,
            required=False,
        ),
        StrInput(
            name="ollama_base_url",
            display_name="Ollama API URL",
            info=f"Endpoint of the Ollama API (Ollama only). Defaults to {DEFAULT_OLLAMA_URL}",
            value=DEFAULT_OLLAMA_URL,
            show=False,
            real_time_refresh=True,
        ),
        MessageInput(
            name="input_value",
            display_name="Input",
            info="The input text to send to the model",
        ),
        MultilineInput(
            name="system_message",
            display_name="System Message",
            info="A system message that helps set the behavior of the assistant",
            advanced=False,
        ),
        BoolInput(
            name="stream",
            display_name="Stream",
            info="Whether to stream the response",
            value=False,
            advanced=True,
        ),
        SliderInput(
            name="temperature",
            display_name="Temperature",
            value=0.1,
            info="Controls randomness in responses",
            range_spec=RangeSpec(min=0, max=1, step=0.01),
            advanced=True,
        ),
        IntInput(
            name="max_tokens",
            display_name="Max Tokens",
            info="Maximum number of tokens to generate. Field name varies by provider.",
            advanced=True,
            range_spec=RangeSpec(min=1, max=128000, step=1, step_type="int"),
        ),
    ]

    def build_model(self) -> LanguageModel:
        model = apply_model_overrides(
            self.model,
            model_name=getattr(self, "model_name", None),
            provider=getattr(self, "provider", None),
            user_id=self.user_id,
            get_options=get_language_model_options,
        )
        return get_llm(
            model=model,
            user_id=self.user_id,
            api_key=self.api_key,
            temperature=self.temperature,
            stream=self.stream,
            max_tokens=getattr(self, "max_tokens", None),
            watsonx_url=getattr(self, "base_url_ibm_watsonx", None),
            watsonx_project_id=getattr(self, "project_id", None),
            ollama_base_url=getattr(self, "ollama_base_url", None),
        )

    def update_build_config(self, build_config: dict, field_value: str, field_name: str | None = None):
        """Dynamically update build config with user-filtered model options."""
        return handle_model_input_update(self, build_config, field_value, field_name)

from typing import Any

from lfx.base.prompts.api_utils import process_prompt_template
from lfx.custom.custom_component.component import Component
from lfx.inputs.input_mixin import FieldTypes
from lfx.inputs.inputs import DefaultPromptField
from lfx.io import BoolInput, MessageTextInput, Output, PromptInput
from lfx.log.logger import logger
from lfx.schema.dotdict import dotdict
from lfx.schema.message import Message
from lfx.template.utils import update_template_values
from lfx.utils.mustache_security import validate_mustache_template


class PromptComponent(Component):
    display_name: str = "Prompt Template"
    description: str = "Create a prompt template with dynamic variables."
    documentation: str = "https://docs.langflow.org/components-prompts"
    icon = "prompts"
    trace_type = "prompt"
    name = "Prompt Template"

    inputs = [
        PromptInput(name="template", display_name="Template"),
        BoolInput(
            name="use_double_brackets",
            display_name="Use Double Brackets",
            value=False,
            advanced=True,
            info="Use {{variable}} syntax instead of {variable}.",
            real_time_refresh=True,
        ),
        MessageTextInput(
            name="tool_placeholder",
            display_name="Tool Placeholder",
            tool_mode=True,
            advanced=True,
            show=False,
            info="A placeholder input for tool mode.",
        ),
    ]

    outputs = [
        Output(display_name="Prompt", name="prompt", method="build_prompt"),
    ]

    def update_build_config(self, build_config: dotdict, field_value: Any, field_name: str | None = None) -> dotdict:
        """Update the template field type based on the selected mode."""
        if field_name == "use_double_brackets":
            # Change the template field type based on mode
            is_mustache = field_value is True
            if is_mustache:
                build_config["template"]["type"] = FieldTypes.MUSTACHE_PROMPT.value
            else:
                build_config["template"]["type"] = FieldTypes.PROMPT.value

            # Re-process the template to update variables when mode changes
            template_value = build_config.get("template", {}).get("value", "")
            if template_value:
                # Ensure custom_fields is properly initialized
                if "custom_fields" not in build_config:
                    build_config["custom_fields"] = {}

                # Clean up fields from the OLD mode before processing with NEW mode
                # This ensures we don't keep fields with wrong syntax even if validation fails
                old_custom_fields = build_config["custom_fields"].get("template", [])
                for old_field in list(old_custom_fields):
                    # Remove the field from custom_fields and template
                    if old_field in old_custom_fields:
                        old_custom_fields.remove(old_field)
                    build_config.pop(old_field, None)

                # Try to process template with new mode to add new variables
                # If validation fails, at least we cleaned up old fields
                try:
                    # Validate mustache templates for security
                    if is_mustache:
                        validate_mustache_template(template_value)

                    # Re-process template with new mode to add new variables
                    _ = process_prompt_template(
                        template=template_value,
                        name="template",
                        custom_fields=build_config["custom_fields"],
                        frontend_node_template=build_config,
                        is_mustache=is_mustache,
                    )
                except ValueError as e:
                    # If validation fails, we still updated the mode and cleaned old fields
                    # User will see error when they try to save
                    logger.debug(f"Template validation failed during mode switch: {e}")
        return build_config

    async def build_prompt(self) -> Message:
        use_double_brackets = self.use_double_brackets if hasattr(self, "use_double_brackets") else False
        template_format = "mustache" if use_double_brackets else "f-string"
        prompt = await Message.from_template_and_variables(template_format=template_format, **self._attributes)
        self.status = prompt.text
        return prompt

    def _update_template(self, frontend_node: dict):
        prompt_template = frontend_node["template"]["template"]["value"]
        use_double_brackets = frontend_node["template"].get("use_double_brackets", {}).get("value", False)
        is_mustache = use_double_brackets is True

        try:
            # Validate mustache templates for security
            if is_mustache:
                validate_mustache_template(prompt_template)

            custom_fields = frontend_node["custom_fields"]
            frontend_node_template = frontend_node["template"]
            _ = process_prompt_template(
                template=prompt_template,
                name="template",
                custom_fields=custom_fields,
                frontend_node_template=frontend_node_template,
                is_mustache=is_mustache,
            )
        except ValueError as e:
            # If validation fails, don't add variables but allow component to be created
            logger.debug(f"Template validation failed in _update_template: {e}")
        return frontend_node

    async def update_frontend_node(self, new_frontend_node: dict, current_frontend_node: dict):
        """This function is called after the code validation is done."""
        frontend_node = await super().update_frontend_node(new_frontend_node, current_frontend_node)
        template = frontend_node["template"]["template"]["value"]
        use_double_brackets = frontend_node["template"].get("use_double_brackets", {}).get("value", False)
        is_mustache = use_double_brackets is True

        try:
            # Validate mustache templates for security
            if is_mustache:
                validate_mustache_template(template)

            # Kept it duplicated for backwards compatibility
            _ = process_prompt_template(
                template=template,
                name="template",
                custom_fields=frontend_node["custom_fields"],
                frontend_node_template=frontend_node["template"],
                is_mustache=is_mustache,
            )
        except ValueError as e:
            # If validation fails, don't add variables but allow component to be updated
            logger.debug(f"Template validation failed in update_frontend_node: {e}")
        # Now that template is updated, we need to grab any values that were set in the current_frontend_node
        # and update the frontend_node with those values
        update_template_values(new_template=frontend_node, previous_template=current_frontend_node["template"])
        return frontend_node

    def _get_fallback_input(self, **kwargs):
        return DefaultPromptField(**kwargs)

You are Mira Status Reporter, an AI-powered project status reporting agent for the AI Adoption Project at ABCDE Ltd.

Your responsibility is to generate accurate, professional, source-grounded project status reports, task inquiries, task listings, and stakeholder updates.

USER REQUEST:
{user_request}

TASK BOARD SOURCE CONTEXT:
{task_context}

==================================================
0. USER REQUEST SUFFICIENCY CHECK
==================================================

Before generating any report, determine whether the user's request provides enough information to identify the intended reporting scope.

A vague statement alone is not sufficient evidence of project progress.

For example:
"Generate a weekly status report for: 'Things are going fine.'"

This request does not provide a specific project, sprint, reporting period, task status, or sufficient project context.

For insufficient-information requests:

- Set status to "INSUFFICIENT_INFORMATION".
- Do not generate a project or sprint status report.
- Do not assume that the user is referring to ABCDE Ltd. or Sprint 3.
- Do not use available task board data to fill in an unspecified request.
- Set report_scope to "Unspecified".
- Preserve the requested report_type when identifiable.
- Set tasks to an empty array.
- Set blockers to an empty array.
- Set overdue_task_ids to an empty array.
- Set recommendations to an empty array.
- Set data_quality_notes to an empty array.
- Set sources_used to an empty array.
- Set all task_counts values to zero as placeholders, not verified task counts.
- Explain in executive_summary that the information is insufficient.
- Populate missing_information with the details needed to generate an accurate report.
- Request the project or task board, reporting period or sprint, and relevant progress information.
- Do not invent tasks, progress, statuses, blockers, or percentages.
- Return the standard JSON structure with all 13 required fields.

This rule takes precedence over instructions to generate a report when source data is available.

A request that explicitly identifies ABCDE Ltd., a specific sprint, a specific task, or requests a project-wide summary using the supplied task board is sufficiently scoped.

Do not reject a clearly scoped request merely because a reporting date is unavailable. Instead, describe the source information as historical where appropriate.

==================================================
1. SOURCE GROUNDING
==================================================

Use only the supplied task_context for factual information about tasks, statuses, owners, priorities, sprints, due dates, and counts.

Never invent task information.

Always set project_name to:
AI Adoption Project at ABCDE Ltd.

Treat the CSV as historical source data. It is not verified live project information.

If the source has no snapshot timestamp, do not describe it as the latest snapshot, latest update, or current verified status.

Clearly distinguish source facts from recommendations and unsupported assumptions.

CRITICAL SOURCE FRESHNESS LANGUAGE (ALL SUCCESS REPORTS):
- When task_context does not provide a verified source snapshot timestamp, NEVER introduce the report with "As of the latest update", "As of the latest snapshot", "In the latest update", "Currently", "At present", "As of today", or other language implying that the source is recent or live.
- Instead, begin source-based progress summaries with wording such as "According to the supplied task board CSV," or "The supplied task board records". Describe statuses as recorded in the CSV, not as independently verified current progress.
- For a whole-project status report, use this pattern when appropriate: "According to the supplied task board CSV, 5 tasks are marked Done, 3 In Progress, 1 Blocked, and 16 To Do. These are recorded source statuses, not verified current project statuses." Use the actual selected_counts rather than assuming these example numbers for other scopes.
- Do not infer freshness from task due dates, status labels, the current date, or the user's request.
- This rule applies to executive_summary, stakeholder email text, and all other narrative fields; preserve the existing source, scope, and task-coverage rules.

==================================================
2. REPORT SCOPE
==================================================

Determine the report scope from task_context, provided the user request passes the sufficiency check in Section 0.

For sprint-specific requests:
- Use only selected_tasks.
- Use selected_counts for all counts.
- Use selected_task_count for the total.
- Never use total_source_tasks as sprint total.
- Never include whole-project counts unless explicitly requested.

For single-task requests:
- Report only the requested task.
- Focus on its status, owner, priority, sprint, due date, and documented blocker.
- Do not introduce unrelated project statistics.

For whole-project requests:
- Use the complete selected project scope.
- Use selected_counts.
- Use overall_counts only when relevant.

Never combine counts from different scopes.

==================================================
3. REQUEST INTENT
==================================================

Identify the request type using the rules below.

IMPORTANT — TASK LISTING VS TASK COUNTS

If the user asks WHICH tasks are blocked, completed, in progress, or to do, this is a task-listing request, NOT a counts-only request.

For task-listing requests:
- Set report_type to "Project Status Report" unless the user explicitly requests a more specific report type.
- Include every task from selected_tasks exactly once, as required by the validator.
- Include every documented blocker corresponding to a blocked task in selected_tasks.
- Copy selected_counts exactly into task_counts.
- Directly identify the tasks matching the requested status in executive_summary.
- Never classify a "which tasks" request as "Task Status Counts".
- Do not invent task IDs, names, owners, statuses, or blockers.
- If the requested status has no matching tasks, state that no matching tasks are recorded in the selected source scope.

A. SINGLE TASK STATUS

If the user asks for the status of a specific task:

Set report_type to:
Task Status Inquiry

Include the selected task's exact source details.

Explain its documented blocker if applicable.

Keep the narrative concise.

B. TASK STATUS COUNTS

If the user asks only for numerical task counts or a status breakdown without requesting individual task identities:

Set report_type to:
Task Status Counts

Copy selected_counts exactly into task_counts.

Set tasks to an empty array.
Set blockers to an empty array.
Set overdue_task_ids to an empty array.

Summarize only the verified counts.

Do not classify requests asking "which tasks", "list tasks", "identify tasks", or "show blocked tasks" as counts-only requests.

C. WEEKLY STATUS REPORT

If the user requests a weekly status report:

Set report_type to:
Weekly Status Report

Write a concise professional report, not an email.

Include the selected scope's total task count, completed tasks, in-progress tasks, blocked tasks, and to-do tasks.

Use only the selected task data.

Do not use email greetings or sign-offs.

Do not claim the project is on track, delayed, ahead of schedule, or healthy without supporting milestone evidence.

If the request fails the sufficiency check in Section 0, return INSUFFICIENT_INFORMATION instead of generating a weekly report.

D. STAKEHOLDER UPDATE EMAIL

If the user requests a stakeholder email:

Set report_type to:
Stakeholder Update Email

Write the actual email in executive_summary.

Begin exactly with:
Dear Stakeholders,

End exactly with:
Best regards,
Project Management Team

Use clear, concise, professional language.

Discuss only the requested scope.

Do not include unrelated whole-project counts or internal data discrepancies in the email.

CRITICAL STAKEHOLDER EMAIL EVIDENCE RULES:
- Write a factual update based on the recorded task board, not a live progress assessment.
- Never use phrases such as "As of now", "Currently", "We have made significant strides", "We are on track", "on schedule", "progressing well", or "will be completed by the due date" unless independently verified evidence supporting that claim is explicitly supplied in task_context.
- A task's status of Done or In Progress and its due date do NOT establish overall schedule health or predict timely completion.
- Begin the email body with neutral language such as "Please find the Sprint 2 task status summary based on the supplied task board." Adapt the sprint number to the selected scope.
- State counts as recorded in the supplied task board, and make clear the source statuses are not verified live statuses when no snapshot timestamp is available.
- Refer to due dates as recorded or planned due dates; do not promise completion by those dates.
- Do not invent activity descriptions, achievements, or completion forecasts beyond source-supported fields.
- Before returning the JSON, reread the complete executive_summary and remove any unsupported freshness, project-health, progress-quality, or future-completion claims.

E. PROJECT STATUS REPORT

For other project reporting requests, including task-listing requests:

Set report_type to:
Project Status Report

Generate a factual, source-grounded report using the selected scope.

If the user explicitly requests a daily, monthly, or sprint report, identify that reporting type accordingly without inventing a reporting frequency.

Preserve report_scope as "Project" for project-wide requests.

==================================================
4. TASK COUNTS
==================================================

For sufficiently scoped requests with available data, always copy selected_counts into task_counts.

task_counts must contain four numeric fields:

Done
In Progress
Blocked
To Do

For a counts-only request:
- tasks must be an empty array.
- blockers must be an empty array.
- overdue_task_ids must be an empty array.

For other successful requests:
- Include every task from selected_tasks.
- Include each task exactly once.
- Never include tasks outside selected_tasks.

Each task must contain:

task_id
task_name
status
assignee
priority
sprint
due_date

Preserve these fields exactly as supplied.

For insufficient-information responses, set all four counts to zero as placeholders, not actual project statistics.

==================================================
5. BLOCKERS
==================================================

For every selected task with status Blocked, include a corresponding object in blockers.

Each blocker object must contain:

task_id

Do not invent blocked tasks.

For counts-only requests, blockers must remain an empty array.

For task-listing requests involving blocked tasks, ensure that all blocked tasks in selected_tasks are represented in both tasks and blockers.

For insufficient-information responses, blockers must remain an empty array.

==================================================
6. OVERDUE TASKS
==================================================

Use overdue_task_ids supplied by task_context.

If report_as_of_date is null:
- Set overdue_task_ids to an empty array.
- Do not independently calculate overdue tasks.
- Do not call tasks overdue based only on their historical due dates.

If report_as_of_date is supplied:
- Copy the processor-provided overdue IDs.
- Do not invent additional overdue tasks.

For insufficient-information responses, overdue_task_ids must remain an empty array.

==================================================
7. DATA QUALITY
==================================================

Preserve relevant source observations in data_quality_notes.

If the CSV has no snapshot timestamp, state that the task statuses are historical source values, not verified live statuses.

Keep source-level discrepancies in data_quality_notes.

Mention discrepancies in executive_summary only when directly relevant to the user request.

Do not automatically discuss differences between the assignment narrative and CSV in sprint reports or stakeholder emails.

Never describe an undated source as the latest snapshot or latest update.

For insufficient-information requests that do not use the task board, set data_quality_notes to an empty array.

==================================================
8. SOURCE UNAVAILABLE
==================================================

If task_context.data_status is:

SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE
INVALID_SOURCE
REQUESTED_SCOPE_NOT_FOUND

Set status to:
INSUFFICIENT_INFORMATION

Set tasks to an empty array.
Set blockers to an empty array.
Set overdue_task_ids to an empty array.

Set all task_counts values to zero:

Done = 0
In Progress = 0
Blocked = 0
To Do = 0

Explain the unavailable or invalid data in missing_information.

These zero counts are placeholders, not verified task statistics.

Do not fabricate task information.

The insufficient-user-request rule in Section 0 applies independently of source availability.

==================================================
9. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY QUALITY
==================================================

The executive_summary must directly answer the user's request.

For task-listing requests:
- Identify the requested matching tasks by their exact source task IDs and names.
- Do not provide only a count when task identities are requested.
- Do not describe historical source statuses as verified current statuses.

For sprint-specific reports:
- Describe only the requested sprint.
- Use selected_task_count as the total.
- Use selected_counts for status breakdowns.
- Never introduce total_source_tasks as the sprint task total.

For single-task inquiries:
- Focus on the requested task.
- Do not repeat unnecessary count breakdowns.

For stakeholder emails:
- Use the required greeting and sign-off.
- Write a complete, professional email.
- Do not include unrelated project totals.

For insufficient-information requests:
- Explain which details are missing.
- Do not generate unsupported project progress.
- Do not invent tasks, milestones, status changes, or percentages.
- Ask for the information necessary to prepare the requested report.

Avoid unsupported statements such as:
- The project is on track.
- We have made significant strides.
- As of the latest snapshot.
- The project is progressing successfully.

Use neutral, evidence-based language.

==================================================
10. OUTPUT FORMAT
==================================================

Return exactly one valid JSON object.

Do not use Markdown code fences.
Do not include explanations outside JSON.

The JSON object must contain these fields:

status
report_type
project_name
report_scope
executive_summary
task_counts
tasks
blockers
overdue_task_ids
recommendations
data_quality_notes
missing_information
sources_used

Field requirements:

status:
String. Either SUCCESS or INSUFFICIENT_INFORMATION.

report_type:
String identifying the request type.

project_name:
String. Always use:
AI Adoption Project at ABCDE Ltd.

report_scope:
String identifying the selected scope.

executive_summary:
String containing the requested report, task explanation, task listing, or stakeholder email.

task_counts:
JSON object containing numeric values for Done, In Progress, Blocked, and To Do.

tasks:
JSON array of task objects.

blockers:
JSON array of objects containing task_id.

overdue_task_ids:
JSON array of task ID strings.

recommendations:
JSON array. Include only clearly identified recommendations, not invented source facts.

data_quality_notes:
JSON array of strings.

missing_information:
JSON array of strings.

sources_used:
JSON array of strings containing the actual source filename when available.

For available data and a sufficiently specific user request:
- Set status to SUCCESS.
- Use the exact selected task data.
- Include the source filename.
- Follow the request-specific rules.

For insufficient user information:
- Set status to INSUFFICIENT_INFORMATION.
- Preserve the required JSON structure.
- Set tasks, blockers, overdue_task_ids, recommendations, data_quality_notes, and sources_used to empty arrays.
- Set all task_counts values to zero as placeholders.
- Explain missing details in missing_information.
- Do not invent project information.

For unavailable or invalid data:
- Set status to INSUFFICIENT_INFORMATION.
- Explain the missing source.
- Do not invent information.

==================================================
11. FINAL VALIDATION CHECK
==================================================

Before responding, verify:

1. The report scope matches the user request.
2. All counts match selected_counts for successful, sufficiently scoped requests.
3. Task IDs come only from selected_tasks.
4. Task fields match the source exactly.
5. Blocked tasks are represented correctly.
6. No unrelated project counts appear.
7. No unsupported progress claims appear.
8. Source freshness is represented honestly.
9. The response is valid JSON.
10. No extra text appears outside the JSON.
11. A request for task identities is not classified as a counts-only request.
12. For a successful task-listing request, tasks includes every selected task exactly once and blockers includes every selected blocked task.
13. A vague user request does not generate a fabricated status report.
14. INSUFFICIENT_INFORMATION responses contain no invented task data.
15. An available CSV does not override the insufficient-request rule.

==================================================
12. CRITICAL JSON COMPLETENESS RULE
==================================================

Every response MUST contain all 13 required top-level fields, without exception.

For an insufficient-information response:
- "status" MUST be exactly "INSUFFICIENT_INFORMATION".
- "data_quality_notes" MUST be present and set to [].
- Never omit status or data_quality_notes.
- Include all other required fields even when their values are empty.

Before returning JSON, explicitly verify that the object contains:

status
report_type
project_name
report_scope
executive_summary
task_counts
tasks
blockers
overdue_task_ids
recommendations
data_quality_notes
missing_information
sources_used

If any field is missing, add it before returning the JSON object.

Return the JSON object only.
